note: Attacker-controlled username from the config JSON 'clients' array is copied into the flexible-array member of a freshly allocated dynsec__client.
A second client with an identical username is inserted into the client hash (uthash HASH_ADD performs no duplicate check), so two hash nodes share the same username key.

During cleanup the lookup keyed on client->username resolves through the bucket chain to the other duplicate node; HASH_DEL then removes that node, not the current client, so the current client is freed while its own node is still linked in data->clients.
The current client object (and the username embedded in it) is released, but its uthash handle remains reachable from the client-list bucket chain.
The HASH_ITER loop advances to the next duplicate client and invokes client__free_item again, which performs another dynsec_clients__find.
The HASH_FIND macro walks the bucket chain whose head still points at the freed client's hh node; reading hashv/keylen/key of the freed node is a heap use-after-free read.
